correctness.rationale: The unique John ellipsoid is invariant under permutation of the n residual coordinates, so in the affine (x_1,u) coordinates it has separate axial radius s and circular radius rho. The end constraints are s<=c and c+s<=h. Each residual coordinate has center (n−c)/n and squared support radius s²/n²+((n−1)/n)rho², giving the sharp feasibility constraint s²+n(n−1)rho²<=(n−c)². For fixed feasible s, lowering c to s preserves feasibility of the end constraints, and maximizes the allowable rho strictly unless c=s. At c=s the volume objective is proportional to s[n(n−2s)]^((n−1)/2), which has its unique unconstrained maximum at s=n/(n+1). The cap imposes s<=h/2, giving both branches and contacts by active supports. The Gram matrix of the restriction of an orthonormal zero-sum embedding to the last n−1 coordinates has determinant 1/n, giving the 1/sqrt(n) volume factor. The logarithmic derivative 1/h−(n−1)/(2(n−h)) vanishes at h_* and its derivative there on the lower branch is negative, proving C¹ and failure of C². The strict inequality in proof line 62 at c=h/2=alpha is a nonessential endpoint slip: the derivative is zero exactly there and positive before it, and the constrained optimum and Finding are unchanged.
residual_risks: No extension to oblique or multiple cuts is assessed. The cited strict derivative slip affects no part of the Finding.

Mordhorst Theorem 6.6 gives a John ellipsoid for a particular simplex-frustum construction, not an all-depth formula. The Godbersen-profile record dda979276949 treats the same geometry but computes opposite-body mixed volumes; the three-phase capped-hypercube record 9b8726b32127 has extra coordinate bounds and is not this family.

evidence: The volume pulls back as κ_n n^n sqrt(p^(n−1)q)=κ_n s rho^(n−1)/sqrt(n). It is constant on the saturation branch, and differentiating the other known branch yields exactly the stated strict increase, matching first derivatives and unequal second derivatives. Setting h=1 gives rho²=1 and volume κ_n/(2sqrt(n)).
The original x_1=0 maps to the upper-sum facet; x_1=h maps to the lower-sum facet; the remaining original facets map to coordinate facets. The contact assertion is thus already in the prior Finding.

evidence: In d34d69923786, the Finding covers F_{n,t}={z_i>=0, t<=sum z_i<=1}, 0<=t<1. The exact map from the frozen K is z=(n−sum x_i,x_2,...,x_n)/n, t=1−h/n. The map is invertible and |det Dz|=n^(−n).

Write H=sum of the prior center coordinates and p,q for its two squared shape eigenvalues. Then x-center coordinate c=n(1−H), s²=n³q and rho²=n²p. Substitution gives both frozen formulas and maps the prior lower-sum contact threshold t_*=(n−1)/(n+1) to h_*=2n/(n+1).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The prior formulas and active hyperplanes agree under the affine map, including the endpoint h=n, and John ellipsoids are affine equivariant. This is exact same-family coverage, not similarity of title or parameter count.

value.rationale: The frustum and its inscribed ellipsoid are natural, but this record delivers no independently useful unknown exact fact beyond the covered geometry. The one-capped arbor instance is a single substitution, the Euclidean volume is an immediate determinant conversion, and the smoothness description is routine differentiation of the known exact branches. The concise optimization is useful as exposition but does not provide a new structural conclusion.
residual_risks: This does not deny the value of the original frustum theorem or of explanatory reformulation; it identifies no separate research finding here.
